We need to propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: steps enumerated forward: 1) Carboxylic acid to amide (coupling). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). 3) Sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthetic steps reverse order: Starting from target, we break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride and aniline? Actually target has sulfonamide linking two aromatic rings: NS(=O)(=O) attached to first ring (para-methyl phenyl) and to second phenyl bearing the unsaturated amide side chain. So retrosynthesis: disconnect sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl fluoride) and amine. Likely sulfonyl chloride derived from sulfonyl chloride (p-tolylsulfonyl chloride) and aniline (the second aromatic amine). So step 3 (retro) yields two fragments: p-tolyl-sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-CH3) and aniline bearing the unsaturated amide side chain: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 (i.e., a phenyl with para position attached to sulfonamide). Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen attached to both rings; after cleavage we get the second aromatic amine (aniline) with the side chain.

Next step: the amide formed from carboxylic acid and amine (aniline). So retro: break amide to give carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The side chain is C(=O)N-aryl. So we get α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to phenyl via double bond: /C=C/C(=O)OH attached to phenyl (the second phenyl). Actually the unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl via the double bond: phenyl-CH=CH-COOH (cinnamic acid). So retro step yields cinnamic acid (p-substituted phenyl) and aniline.

Third step: Doebner modification: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid). So retro: break cinnamic acid to give aromatic aldehyde (benzaldehyde) and malonic acid. The aldehyde is the phenyl ring (c3ccccc3) which is the same as aniline? Wait the aniline is attached to the amide nitrogen, not the aldehyde. The Doebner modification forms the α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl (cinnamic acid). The aldehyde is the same phenyl ring (c3ccccc3). So retro: cinnamic acid -> benzaldehyde + malonic acid.

Thus overall three steps:

Step1 (retro): target -> sulfonyl chloride + aniline with side chain (cinnamoyl aniline). Step2 (retro): aniline side chain -> cinnamic acid + aniline (the same aniline? Actually the amide nitrogen attaches to aniline (c3ccccc3N). So after breaking amide we get cinnamic acid and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Step3 (retro): cinnamic acid -> benzaldehyde + malonic acid.

Now we need to find templates for each step. We have template 401931 which seems to be amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine -> amide with double bond). That matches step2 (amide formation). So we can use template_id 401931 for step2.

We need a template for sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). Search maybe returns none. Could try search with functional_groups_formed ["sulfonamides"] but got empty. Maybe need to specify functional_groups_broken ["sulfonyl chloride"]? Let's try.
